To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultrasonic treatment increases the green emission intensity of ZnO nanostructures.
sonochemical route is a promising method for the synthesis of ZnO nanostructures and the UV luminescence of ZnO is strongly dependent on the surface defects.
sonochemically synthesized ZnO nanostructures have shown a green emission in visible region and the intensity of the green emission was enhanced by the ultrasonic post-treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of cauliflower-like ZnO nanocrystals with surface 1 D nanoarrays and the study of their PL properties.
the synthesis of ZnO nanomaterials and their application in the field of ultrasonic technology.
the sonochemical synthesis of ZnO nanostructures, which can be used in various opto-electronic applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ultrasonic irradiation can be used as an effective tool to modify the surface properties of the nanostructures.
the ultrasonic post-treatment is an effective way to increase the surface defects and hence to enhance the visible emission in the sonochemically prepared ZnO nanostructures.
the sonochemical method is a very promising and simple technique for the synthesis of ZnO nanostructures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ultrasonic irradiation of ZnO nanostructures can be used as a new and simple approach for the modification of the surface properties of the ZnO nanostructures.
the ultrasonic treatment of the ZnO particles is a very effective and convenient method to tune their PL emission.
the sonochemically synthesized ZnO nanostructures have a great potential for optoelectronic applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ultrasonic post-treatment is an easy, fast and effective way to tune the optical properties of ZnO nanostructures.
the ultrasonic treatment of the particles can be used for the tuning of the surface defects of ZnO nanostructures and thus the PL emission intensity of the samples.
the ultrasonic irradiation can be a useful method for controlling the surface properties of ZnO nanostructures.
